'''Artem R. Oganov''' (born 3 March 1975) is a Russian theoretical crystallographer, mineralogist, [[Chemists of Russia|chemist]], [[List of Russian physicists|physicist]], and materials scientist.<ref>[http://uspex-team.org Oganov's laboratory site]. Uspex-team.org. Retrieved on 25 March 2018.</ref> He is known mostly for his works on computational materials discovery and [[crystal structure prediction]], studies of matter at extreme conditions, including matter of planetary interiors.

== Education ==

Oganov graduated from [[Moscow State University]] in 1997 with magna summa cum laude and diploma in Crystallography and Crystal Chemistry. In 2002 he obtained a PhD degree in Crystallography from University College London, and in 2007 got a Habilitation degree from [[ETH Zurich]].

== Career ==

In 2008–2017 he was a professor at [[Stony Brook University]]. In 2012 Oganov received the "1000 talents" professorship in China. In 2013, having won a megagrant awarded by the Russian Government, Oganov opened a laboratory at [[Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://mipt.ru/en/news/Artem_Oganov_opens_a_laboratory_of_computer_design_of_materials_at_MIPT | title=Artem Oganov opens a laboratory of computer design of materials at MIPT|publisher=adapted from Moscow Region News|date=5 June 2013}}</ref> Since 2015 he is a Professor (since 2024 - Distinguished Professor) at [[Skolkovo Institute of Science and Technology]].

== Awards and honours ==

He is a laureate of several prestigious awards, including an ETH Latsis Prize,<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.ethz.ch/content/dam/ethz/main/research/pdf/latsis-prize/2014_Latsis_Laureates.pdf |title=List of ETH Latsis Prize Laureates |access-date=15 August 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151018093352/https://www.ethz.ch/content/dam/ethz/main/research/pdf/latsis-prize/2014_Latsis_Laureates.pdf |archive-date=18 October 2015 }}</ref> Research Excellence Model of the European Mineralogical Union.<ref>[http://eurominunion.org/?page_id=213 2007 Research Excellence Medal]. Eurominunion.org. Retrieved on 25 March 2018.</ref> In 2012, Oganov won a "1000 talents professor" title in China and in the same year became a Professor Honoris Causa of Yanshan University (China), in 2013 elected Fellow of the Mineralogical Association of America,<ref>[http://www.minsocam.org/MSA/Awards/Fellowslist.html List of MSA Fellows]. Minsocam.org. Retrieved on 25 March 2018.</ref> In 2016 and 2017 he was named as one of the most cited Russian scientists in Chemistry <ref>[https://indicator.ru/news/2016/12/08/vrucheny-nagrady-samym-citiruemy-rossijskim-issledovatelyam/ 2016 Russian Highly Cited Researcher Award] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170921051503/https://indicator.ru/news/2016/12/08/vrucheny-nagrady-samym-citiruemy-rossijskim-issledovatelyam/ |date=21 September 2017 }}. Indicator.ru. Retrieved on 25 March 2018.</ref> and Physics,<ref>[http://info.clarivate.com/rcis_blog_2018_02_15_russia_web_of_science_awards_2017/ Clarivate Analytics awarded highly cited Russian researchers ]. Clarivate.com. Retrieved on 25 March 2018.</ref> respectively. In 2022, 2024 and 2025 he was included in the list of Highly Cited Researchers ([[Clarivate]]).<ref>[https://clarivate.com/highly-cited-researchers/ Highly Cited Researchers]</ref> He was elected a Fellow of the [[International Core Academy of Sciences and Humanities]] in 2024.,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Anna |date=2024-04-15 |title=Scientist Artem Oganov elected to International Core Academy of Sciences and Humanities |url=https://alphanews.am/en/scientist-artem-oganov-elected-to-international-core-academy-of-sciences-and-humanities/ |access-date=2025-07-16 |website=Alphanews |language=en-US}}</ref> in 2025 becoming a member of its Academic Council.

In 2017 he was awarded the Gamow prize <ref>[https://indicator.ru/news/2017/10/24/kabanov-i-oganov-premiya-rasa/ Kabanov and Oganov won the Gamow award] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171207084711/https://indicator.ru/news/2017/10/24/kabanov-i-oganov-premiya-rasa/ |date=7 December 2017 }}. Indicator.ru. Retrieved on 25 March 2018.</ref> and Concord prize,<ref>[http://www.sarinfo.org/sarnews/04-12-17.shtml Concord prize award] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171207084010/http://www.sarinfo.org/sarnews/04-12-17.shtml |date=7 December 2017 }}. Sarinfo.org. Retrieved on 25 March 2018.</ref> In 2019, he received the [[Friendship Award]],<ref>[https://www.skoltech.ru/en/2019/10/skoltech-professor-artem-oganov-is-honored-with-the-chinese-friendship-award/ Oganov receives the Friendship Award]</ref> the highest award given by Chinese government to foreign experts. In 2015 Oganov was elected [[Professor of the Russian Academy of Sciences]].,<ref>[http://www.ras.ru/presidium/documents/directions.aspx?ID=d970afa6-9c0c-4d0c-9c0b-cde1155d0b73 Elected Professors of RAS]. Ras.ru (29 December 2015). Retrieved on 25 March 2018.</ref> and in 2017 he became a member <ref name="ae-info1"/> of the Academy of Europe [[Academia Europaea]], and in 2020 elected Fellow of the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]]<ref>[https://www.skoltech.ru/en/2020/04/skoltech-professor-artem-oganov-elected-fellow-of-the-royal-society-of-chemistry/ Oganov elected Fellow of the RSC]</ref> and Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]].<ref>[https://www.skoltech.ru/en/2020/09/artem-r-oganov-elected-american-physical-society-fellow/ Oganov elected Fellow of the APS]</ref> In 2011 he founded the Commission on Crystallography of Materials at the [[International Union of Crystallography]], which he chaired until 2017. In 2017-2020 he served as a member of the Presidential council for science and education.<ref>[http://www.kremlin.ru/structure/members/6 Presidential council for science and education]. Kremlin.ru (1 January 1991). Retrieved on 25 March 2018.</ref> In 2021-2024 he was a chairman of the Department of Semiconductors and Dielectrics of [[MISIS]]<ref>{{cite web | url=https://mpid.misis.ru/en/ | title=МПиД – кафедра материаловедения полупроводников и диэлектриков НИТУ "МИСИС" – Кафедра материаловедения полупроводников и диэлектриков НИТУ "МИСИС" }}</ref> and head of the newly founded Laboratory of Crystal Chemistry of the Institute of [[Geochemistry]] and Analytical Chemistry of [[Russian Academy of Sciences]].

Oganov has held over 10 invited professorships (Universita degli Studi di Milano, Lille'Polytech, University of Paris, University of Poitiers, Chinese University of Hong Kong, [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]], Japan Society for the Promotion of Science, etc.).  In 2011, Forbes magazine listed Oganov among "50 Russians who conquered the world".<ref>[https://themoscowtimes.com/news/forbes-gives-50-reasons-to-stay-in-russia-10359 Forbes names 50 Russians who "conquered" the world]. Themoscowtimes.com (25 October 2011). Retrieved on 25 March 2018.</ref>  In 2012, highly acclaimed cinema director, Laureate of State Prize Vladimir Gerchikov made a film "The color of a crystal" about Oganov,<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rsJzd53UXz0 «The color of a crystal»]. YouTube.com (25 October 2015). Retrieved on 25 March 2018.</ref> in 2015 the celebrated TV journalist [[Leonid Parfenov]] made a film "Made by Russians" about him.<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oFEmUJgWHMU Made by Russians]. YouTube.com (14 September 2015). Retrieved on 25 March 2018</ref> and two other films about him appeared in 2018 on Kultura-TV channel <ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9g_t-RZNYuA Artem Oganov (the TV-film)]. YouTube.com (19 October 2018)</ref> and on NTV channel <ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4ybyVff9by4&t=136s Cool Story: Return of the Professor].</ref> In 2019, as part of the 150th commemoration of Mendeleev's Periodic Table, yet another film came out,<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YMoqH32qWmc A New Element of the Russian Table]</ref> where Oganov is one of the central characters. In 2013, magazines "Russian reporter" and "Expert" have listed Oganov among 100 most influential Russians today.<ref>[http://www.rusrep.ru/article/2014/10/30/100-lyudej-sovremennoj-rossii/ 100 people of modern Russia]. Rusrep.ru. Retrieved on 25 March 2018.</ref>

== Research ==

Oganov has published over 300 peer-reviewed articles (many in top journals, e.g. Nature, Science) and book chapters and 5 patents. He is a coauthor of 3 monographs and the author of 1 popular science book. His works have >43500 citations, h-index 100 (Google scholar, as of November 2025).<ref>[https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=1aqQ8ioAAAAJ&hl=en Google scholar citation]. Scholar.google.com. Retrieved on 12 November 2025.</ref>

His most important works are in fields of computational materials discovery, in particular the effects of pressure on chemical bonding, and state of matter at extreme conditions (e.g. inside the Earth and other planets). He has developed novel and highly efficient methods of crystal structure prediction <ref>{{cite journal|vauthors=Oganov AR, Glass CW |title=Crystal structure prediction using ab initio evolutionary techniques: principles and applications |journal=[[Journal of Chemical Physics]]|volume=124|issue=24 |year=2006|article-number=244704|doi=10.1063/1.2210932|pmid=16821993|bibcode=2006JChPh.124x4704O |arxiv=0911.3186|s2cid=9688132 }}</ref> that became basis of the USPEX code,<ref>[http://uspex-team.org USPEX code site]. Uspex-team.org. Retrieved on 30 January 2022.</ref> used by more than 8500 researchers worldwide. Among the highlights are the discovery of the structure of a superhard phase of boron, gamma-B,<ref>{{cite journal|vauthors= Oganov AR, Chen J, Gatti C, Ma YZ, Ma YM, Glass CW, Liu Z, Yu T, Kurakevych OO, Solozhenko VL |title=Ionic high-pressure form of elemental boron |journal=[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]|volume=457|issue=7231 |year=2009|pages=863–867|doi=10.1038/nature07736|pmid=19182772|bibcode=2009Natur.457..863O |arxiv=0911.3192|s2cid=4412568 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.nytimes.com/2009/02/03/science/03boron.html | title=Theory and Experiment Meet, and a New Form of Boron Is Found | work=New York Times | date=2 February 2009 | access-date=9 February 2015 | author=Chang, Kenneth}}</ref> transparent phase of sodium,<ref>{{cite journal|vauthors=Ma Y, Eremets MI, Oganov AR, Xie Y, Trojan I, Medvedev S, Lyakhov AO, Valle M, Prakapenka V |title=Transparent dense sodium |journal=[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]|volume=458|issue=7235 |year=2009|pages=182–185|doi=10.1038/nature07786|pmid=19279632 |bibcode=2009Natur.458..182M |arxiv=0911.3190|s2cid=11861834 }}</ref> new carbon allotrope,<ref>{{cite journal|vauthors=Li Q, Ma Y, Oganov AR, Wang H, Wang H, Xu Y, Cui T, Mao HK, Zou G |s2cid=18612210 |title=Superhard monoclinic polymorph of carbon |journal=[[Physical Review Letters]]|volume=102|issue=17 |year=2009|article-number=175506|doi=10.1103/physrevlett.102.175506|pmid=19518796|bibcode=2009PhRvL.102q5506L }}</ref> prediction of MgSiO<sub>3</sub> post-perovskite and its stability in the Earth's mantle,<ref>{{cite journal|vauthors=Oganov AR, Ono S |title=Theoretical and experimental evidence for a post-perovskite phase of MgSiO3 in Earth's D" layer |journal=Nature|volume=430|issue=6998 |year=2004|pages=445–448|doi=10.1038/nature02701|pmid=15269766|bibcode=2004Natur.430..445O |arxiv=0911.3184|s2cid=4418049 }}</ref> prediction of other planet-forming minerals,<ref>{{cite journal|vauthors=Li HF, Oganov AR, Cui H, Zhou XF, Dong X, Wang HT |title=Ultrahigh-pressure magnesium hydrosilicates as reservoirs of water in early Earth|journal=[[Physical Review Letters]]|year=2022|volume=128| issue=3 |article-number=035703| doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.128.035703 | pmid=35119889 | arxiv=2202.00752 | bibcode=2022PhRvL.128c5703L | s2cid=246190557 }}</ref> prediction and synthesis of "forbidden" compounds (e.g., Na<sub>3</sub>Cl),<ref>{{cite journal|vauthors= Zhang WW, Oganov AR, Goncharov AF, Zhu Q, Boulfelfel SE, Lyakhov AO, Stavrou E, Somayazulu M, Prakapenka VB, Konopkova Z |title=Unexpected stoichiometries of stable sodium chlorides |journal=[[Science (journal)|Science]]|volume=342|issue=6165 |year=2013|pages=1502–1505|doi=10.1126/science.1244989|pmid=24357316|bibcode=2013Sci...342.1502Z |arxiv=1310.7674|s2cid=15298372 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=http://phys.org/news/2013-12-salty-ordinary-table-salt-forbidden.html | title=Salty surprise: Ordinary table salt turns into 'forbidden' forms | work=[[Phys.org]] | date=19 December 2013 | access-date=9 February 2015}}</ref> discovery of helium chemistry,<ref>{{cite journal|vauthors=Dong X, Oganov AR, Goncharov AF, Stavrou E, Lobanov S, Saleh G, Qian GR, Zhu Q, Gatti C, Deringer VL, Dronskowski R, Zhou XF, Prakapenka VB, Konôpková Z, Popov IA, Boldyrev AI, Wang HT |title= A stable compound of helium and sodium at high pressure |journal=Nature Chemistry |volume= 9 |issue= 5 |pages= 440–445 |year=2017 |doi=10.1038/nchem.2716|pmid= 28430195 |bibcode=2017NatCh...9..440D |arxiv=1309.3827 |s2cid= 20459726 }}</ref> and creation of borophene - a 2D-monolayer of boron atoms, with great promises for future technologies.<ref>{{cite journal|vauthors=Mannix AJ, Zhou XF, Kiraly B, Wood JD, Alducin D, Myers BD, Liu X, Fisher BL, Santiago U, Guest JR, Yacaman MJ, Ponce A, Oganov journal|vauthors=Tantardini C, Oganov AR |title=Thermochemical electronegativities of the elements|journal=[[Nature Communications]]| year=2021 |volume=12| issue=1 |article-number=2087| doi=10.1038/s41467-021-22429-0 | doi-access=free| pmid=33828104 | pmc=8027013 | bibcode=2021NatCo..12.2087T }}</ref>

Extending the definition of electronegativity to high pressures and tabulating [[electronegativities]] and [[chemical hardness]] for all elements (up to Cm, #96), Oganov and colleagues were able to explain many unusual phenomena of high pressure chemistry, as well as predicting new phenomena and compounds.<ref>{{cite journal|title= Electronegativity and chemical hardness of elements under pressure.|vauthors=Dong X, Oganov AR, Cui H, Zhou XF, Wang HT |journal= [[Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences]] |year= 2022|volume= 119|issue= 10|article-number= e2117416119|doi= 10.1073/pnas.2117416119|doi-access=free |pmid= 35238642|pmc= 8915985|arxiv= 1503.00230|bibcode= 2022PNAS..11917416D}}</ref> Prediction of the new high pressure hydrous compound Mg<sub>2</sub>SiO<sub>5</sub>H<sub>2</sub> has inspired a new hypothesis on the origin of the Earth's [[hydrosphere]].<ref>{{cite journal|vauthors=Li HF, Oganov AR, Cui H, Zhou XF, Dong X, Wang HT |title= Ultrahigh-pressure magnesium hydrosilicates as reservoirs of water in early Earth. |journal= Physical Review Letters|year= 2022 | volume= 128|issue= 3 | article-number= 035703|doi= == Personal life and family ==

Oganov speaks 5 languages (Russian, English, French, German, and Italian), is married, has four children and is a parishioner of St. Louis Catholic Church in Moscow.<ref>[http://xn--80aqecdrlilg.xn--p1ai/artyom-oganov-budushhee-est-tolko-u-teh-kto-v-nego-verit/ Артем Оганов: "Будущее есть только у тех, кто в него верит"]. http://рускатолик.рф (22 November 2013)</ref> His mother is Jewish and his father is Armenian.<ref>{{Cite web |title=HED_people. Artem Romaevich Oganov - latest articles on hedclub.com – Higher Education Discovery |url=https://hedclub.com/en/publication/hed_people_artem_romaevich_oganov_173 |access-date=2025-08-17 |website=hedclub.com}}</ref>
